title: Global View - The Night Before Christmas
audio: mp3/337. Global View - The Night Before Christmas.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and a very Merry Christmas to everyone.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，祝大家圣诞快乐。

segments.en: That's right, Merry Christmas. We are at that time again where we are celebrating Christmas, we're having dinner with family and friends, we're giving presents and of course, there are some other traditions that come into play like for example Santa Claus.
segments.zh: 没错，圣诞快乐。 当时我们又在庆祝圣诞节，我们正在与家人和朋友共进晚餐，我们正在赠送礼物，当然还有其他一些传统可以发挥作用，例如圣诞老人。

segments.en: Santa Claus.
segments.zh: 圣诞老人。

segments.en: So, we've got a very special advanced level lesson for you today.
segments.zh: 所以，我们今天为您准备了一堂非常特别的高级课程。

segments.en: We've got a poem.
segments.zh: 我们有一首诗。

segments.en: It's a very traditional poem that is read or listened to on the holiday and we're going to talk a little bit about some of the interesting words and phrases that are used in this.
segments.zh: 这是一首非常传统的诗歌，在假期被阅读或听过，我们将谈谈一些有趣的单词和短语。

segments.en: But first off, let's just listen to the poem itself.
segments.zh: 但首先，让我们听诗本身。

segments.en: 'Twas the night before Christmas, when all through the house, not a creature was stirring, not even a mouse.
segments.zh: 圣诞前夜，整座屋子静悄悄，连一只老鼠都没有动静。

segments.en: The stockings were hung by the chimney with care, in hopes that St. Nicholas soon would be there.
segments.zh: 长袜被仔细挂在烟囱旁，盼着圣尼古拉斯快快到来。

segments.en: The children were nestled all snug in their beds, while visions of sugarplums danced in their heads.
segments.zh: 孩子们舒舒服服地睡在床上，梦里的糖李子翩翩起舞。

segments.en: And Mama in her kerchief and I in my cap had just settled down for a long winter's nap.
segments.zh: 妈妈裹着头巾，我戴着睡帽，刚躺下准备睡个漫长的冬夜觉。

segments.en: When out on the lawn there arose such a clatter, I sprang from the bed to see what was the matter.
segments.zh: 草坪上突然传来一阵喧闹，我从床上一跃而起，想看个究竟。

segments.en: Away to the window I flew like a flash, tore open the shutters and threw open the sash.
segments.zh: 我闪电般冲到窗边，猛地推开百叶窗，拉起窗框。

segments.en: The moon on the breast of the new-fallen snow gave the lustre of midday to objects below.
segments.zh: 月光洒在新落的雪上，把下方的景物照得像正午一样明亮。

segments.en: When what to my wondering eyes should appear but a miniature sleigh and eight tiny reindeer,
segments.zh: 这时我惊奇地看见一辆小雪橇和八只小驯鹿，

segments.en: with a little old driver so lively and quick, I knew in a moment it must be St. Nick.
segments.zh: 驾车的是位活泼敏捷的小老头，我立刻知道那是圣尼克。

segments.en: More rapid than eagles his coursers they came, and he whistled and shouted and called them by name.
segments.zh: 驯鹿快过雄鹰奔来，他吹着口哨，高声喊出它们的名字。

segments.en: Now Dasher, now Dancer, now Prancer and Vixen, on Comet, on Cupid, on Donder and Blitzen!
segments.zh: “Dasher、Dancer、Prancer、Vixen！Comet、Cupid、Donder、Blitzen！”

segments.en: To the top of the porch, to the top of the wall! Now dash away, dash away, dash away all!
segments.zh: “冲上门廊顶，跃上高墙顶！飞吧，飞吧，全都飞起来！”

segments.en: As dry leaves that before the wild hurricanes fly, when they meet with an obstacle, mount to the sky.
segments.zh: 它们像狂风中翻飞的枯叶，遇到障碍便腾上天空。

segments.en: So up to the housetop the coursers they flew with the sleigh full of toys, and St. Nicholas too.
segments.zh: 驯鹿拉着满载玩具的雪橇，连同圣尼古拉斯一起飞上屋顶。

segments.en: And then in a twinkling I heard on the roof the prancing and pawing of each little hoof.
segments.zh: 转眼间，我听见屋顶上传来小蹄子轻快的奔踏声。

segments.en: As I drew in my head and was turning around, down the chimney St. Nicholas came with a bound.
segments.zh: 我刚把头缩回来、转过身，圣尼古拉斯就一跃而下，从烟囱里钻了出来。

segments.en: He was dressed all in fur from his head to his toe, and his clothes were all tarnished with ashes and soot.
segments.zh: 他从头到脚裹着毛皮，衣服沾满了灰烬和煤烟。

segments.en: A bundle of toys he had flung on his back, and he looked like a peddler just opening his pack.
segments.zh: 他背着一大袋玩具，像个刚打开货包的小贩。

segments.en: His eyes, how they twinkled! His dimples, how merry!
segments.zh: 他的眼睛闪闪发亮，酒窝里满是笑意。

segments.en: His cheeks were like roses, his nose like a cherry.
segments.zh: 他的双颊红如玫瑰，鼻子红如樱桃。

segments.en: His droll little mouth was drawn up in a bow, and the beard of his chin was as white as the snow.
segments.zh: 他俏皮的小嘴弯成弓形，下巴上的胡子白得像雪。

segments.en: The stump of a pipe he held tight in his teeth, and the smoke it encircled his head like a wreath.
segments.zh: 他嘴里叼着短烟斗，烟雾像花环一样绕着头。

segments.en: He had a broad face and a little round belly that shook when he laughed like a bowl full of jelly.
segments.zh: 他有张宽脸和圆鼓鼓的小肚子，一笑起来就像一碗果冻般颤动。

segments.en: He was chubby and plump, a right old jolly elf, and I laughed when I saw him in spite of myself.
segments.zh: 他又圆又胖，是个快活的老精灵；我见了他，也忍不住笑了。

segments.en: A wink of his eye and a twist of his head soon gave me to know I had nothing to dread.
segments.zh: 他眨眨眼、歪歪头，立刻让我知道无需害怕。

segments.en: He spoke not a word but went straight to work and filled all the stockings, then turned with a jerk.
segments.zh: 他一句话也没说，径直忙起活来，把长袜塞满，然后猛地转身。

segments.en: And laying his finger aside of his nose and giving a nod, up the chimney he rose.
segments.zh: 他把手指放在鼻边，点点头，便从烟囱升了上去。

segments.en: He sprang to his sleigh, to his team gave a whistle, and away they all flew like the down of a thistle.
segments.zh: 他跃上雪橇，向驯鹿吹声口哨，大家像蓟花绒毛一样飘飞远去。

segments.en: But I heard him exclaim ere as he drove out of sight, Happy Christmas to all, and to all a good night!
segments.zh: 他消失在视线前，我听见他高声喊道：“祝大家圣诞快乐，晚安！”

segments.en: Alright, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So, the poem is very nice.
segments.zh: 所以，这首诗非常好听。

segments.en: It's long.
segments.zh: 它很长。

segments.en: And just to kind of recap what the poem is talking about, what is the general story of the poem?
segments.zh: 只是为了回顾这首诗在说什么，这首诗的一般故事是什么？

segments.en: The story of the poem is that Santa Claus is coming to visit someone's house.
segments.zh: 这首诗的故事是圣诞老人要来拜访某人的房子。

segments.en: And there's a person in the story who is watching Santa Claus arrive.
segments.zh: 故事中有一个人正在观看圣诞老人的到来。

segments.en: And he's seeing Santa Claus take the reindeer up onto the roof, come down the chimney, and lay the presents out for the children, filling the stockings as well.
segments.zh: 他看到圣诞老人把驯鹿带到屋顶上，从烟囱里下来，把礼物送给孩子们，也把长袜装满了。

segments.en: Okay, so it's basically a nice poetic description of Santa Claus.
segments.zh: 好的，所以它基本上是对圣诞老人的诗意描述。

segments.en: And also, it goes in to describe in a very nice way the way Santa Claus looks like.
segments.zh: 而且，它以一种非常好的方式描述了圣诞老人的样子。

segments.en: It's very descriptive. We have descriptions of what Santa Claus looks like, what he's wearing, his smile, how he's a little bit fat.
segments.zh: 这是非常描述性的。 我们有描述圣诞老人的样子，他穿什么，他的笑容，他有点胖。

segments.en: We also have descriptions of the animals, the special animals that we hear about so often that are called reindeer.
segments.zh: 我们也有动物的描述，我们经常听到的特殊动物被称为驯鹿。

segments.en: Alright, so we've divided up the poem by lines, so then it's going to be easier for you to go to the line that we're talking about.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们把这首诗分成了几行，所以你更容易去我们正在谈论的行。

segments.en: Let's start with the first line, with this first word that's actually very interesting.
segments.zh: 让我们从第一行开始，第一个单词实际上很有趣。

segments.en: "'Twas the night before Christmas when all through the house."
segments.zh: “那是圣诞节的前一天晚上，整个房子都在。”

segments.en: So what does this first word mean?
segments.zh: 那么第一个字是什么意思呢？

segments.en: "'Twas' is an abbreviation, so it's a shortened version of, it was.
segments.zh: “'Twas'是一个缩写，所以它是一个缩写的版本。

segments.en: Okay, so, but do you actually use this now if you're writing?
segments.zh: 好吧，但是，如果你正在写作，你现在真的使用它吗？

segments.en: No, this is not something I would use now in writing, and it's not something I would say.
segments.zh: 不，这不是我现在以书面形式使用的东西，也不是我会说的。

segments.en: It's actually more of an archaic form, something that you might hear in poetry or historical writing.
segments.zh: 它实际上更像是一种古老的形式，你可能会在诗歌或历史写作中听到。

segments.en: Okay, so it was the night before Christmas, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，那是圣诞节的前一天晚上，对吧？

segments.en: So we're talking about December 24th.
segments.zh: 所以我们谈论的是 12 月 24 日。

segments.en: The night of December 24th, that's right.
segments.zh: 12 月 24 日晚上，没错。

segments.en: Alright, so the first two lines talk about how it was the night before Christmas and in the house there was nothing stirring, not even a mouse.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以前两行都在谈论圣诞节前一天晚上的情况，房子里没有任何东西，甚至没有老鼠。

segments.en: So not even the smallest little animal, so it's very quiet in the house is what's happening.
segments.zh: 所以即使是最小的小动物也不是，所以房子里很安静是正在发生的事情。

segments.en: So now we jump to line number seven, where the poet describes, "'And Mama in her kerchief and I in my cap.'"
segments.zh: 所以现在我们跳到第七行，诗人在那里描述了“'和妈妈在她的头巾和我的帽子里。'”

segments.en: So we know that the person talking is the dad, because he's talking about himself and Mama, mother.
segments.zh: 所以我们知道说话的人是爸爸，因为他在谈论他自己和妈妈，妈妈。

segments.en: They're in bed together.
segments.zh: 他们一起在床上。

segments.en: "'And Mama in her kerchief and I in my cap.'"
segments.zh: “‘还有妈妈在她的头巾上，我戴着帽子。’”

segments.en: So I'm wearing a nightcap, a cover on my head, it's like a hat.
segments.zh: 所以我戴着睡帽，头上戴了一个套，就像一顶帽子。

segments.en: "'And Mama has a kerchief.'"
segments.zh: “‘妈妈有一条头巾。’”

segments.en: What's a kerchief?
segments.zh: 什么是头巾？

segments.en: A kerchief is another abbreviation, it's short for handkerchief.
segments.zh: 头巾是另一个缩写，是手帕的缩写。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And a handkerchief is a piece of fabric or cloth that sometimes we use for our noses when we have to blow our nose.
segments.zh: 手帕是一块织物或布，有时我们在不得不擤鼻子时将其用于鼻子。

segments.en: But also you can use a kerchief in your hair to cover your hair.
segments.zh: 但你也可以用头发上的头巾遮住头发。

segments.en: Okay, so if you can imagine it, this must take place, I don't know, maybe 50, 60 years ago when dads used to wear hats to bed and women also handkerchiefs on their heads.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果你能想象的话，这一定是发生了，我不知道，也许是 50、60 年前，当爸爸们经常戴帽子睡觉时，女人的头上也戴着手帕。

segments.en: Maybe 200 years ago when people wore these long night hats, nightcaps.
segments.zh: 也许 200 年前，当人们戴着这些长夜帽、睡帽时。

segments.en: The pajamas and everything.
segments.zh: 睡衣和一切。

segments.en: All right, now let's jump over to line 18 and 19 when he's talking about the reindeer and the sleigh arriving and he says, "'I knew in a moment it must be Saint Nick.'"
segments.zh: 好吧，现在让我们跳到 18 号线和 19 号线，当他谈论驯鹿和雪橇到达时，他说：“我一会儿就知道它一定是圣尼克。”

segments.en: This is another way of calling Santa Claus, right?
segments.zh: 这是给圣诞老人打电话的另一种方式，对吧？

segments.en: Saint Nicholas is his name, but you also call him Claus or Santa Claus.
segments.zh: 圣尼古拉斯是他的名字，但你也叫他克劳斯或圣诞老人。

segments.en: Okay, and then he said, "'More rapid than eagles, his coursers they came.'"
segments.zh: 好吧，然后他说，“‘比老鹰快，他们来了他的课程。’”

segments.en: So the word order is a bit strange here.
segments.zh: 所以这里的单词顺序有点奇怪。

segments.en: This is common in poetry.
segments.zh: 这在诗歌中很常见。

segments.en: We could also say, "'His coursers came more rapidly than eagles.'
segments.zh: 我们也可以说，“‘他的课程家的来得比老鹰快。’

segments.en: They were very, very fast."
segments.zh: 他们非常非常快。”

segments.en: But what are these coursers? We're talking about the animals pulling Santa Claus.
segments.zh: 但这些课程是什么？ 我们说的是动物拉圣诞老人。

segments.en: And what are those animals again?
segments.zh: 那些动物又是什么？

segments.en: They're called reindeer.
segments.zh: 他们被称为驯鹿。

segments.en: Reindeer.
segments.zh: 驯鹿。

segments.en: So the reindeer are very, very fast.
segments.zh: 所以驯鹿非常非常快。

segments.en: Okay, that's right because he's making the comparison about how fast eagles are compared to them.
segments.zh: 好吧，这是对的，因为他正在比较老鹰与它们的速度有多快。

segments.en: And we hear their names, right?
segments.zh: 我们听到他们的名字，对吧？

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: He goes on to say, "'Now Dasher, now Dancer, now Prancer.'"
segments.zh: 他接着说：“‘现在达舍，现在是舞者，现在是跳马者。’”

segments.en: And all of their names, Vixen, Comet, Cupid, Donder, and Blitzen.
segments.zh: 以及他们所有的名字，狐狸精、彗星、丘比特、唐德和布尔岑。

segments.en: All eight reindeer.
segments.zh: 八只驯鹿。

segments.en: Each animal has its own name.
segments.zh: 每只动物都有自己的名字。

segments.en: That's right. So all eight reindeer.
segments.zh: 没错。 所以八只驯鹿。

segments.en: Actually, we're missing one though that's very common nowadays.
segments.zh: 实际上，我们错过了一种，尽管现在很常见。

segments.en: The reindeer that goes in the front lighting, illuminating the sky.
segments.zh: 前方灯光下的驯鹿照亮天空。

segments.en: Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer. You might know the song, "'Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer.'"
segments.zh: 鲁道夫红鼻子驯鹿。 你可能知道这首歌，“‘鲁道夫红鼻子驯鹿。’”

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So there are actually nine reindeer nowadays, but I guess this story was before the Rudolph story came out.
segments.zh: 所以现在实际上有九只驯鹿，但我想这个故事是在鲁道夫故事出来之前。

segments.en: This is interesting because those are the names of all the reindeer.
segments.zh: 这很有趣，因为这些是所有驯鹿的名字。

segments.en: Now, I'm not sure in which order they are. I don't know who's in the back, who's in the front.
segments.zh: 现在，我不确定它们的顺序。 不知道后面是谁，谁在前面。

segments.en: I don't know either, but it's important to know that they're very fast, and they come down, and then they go up.
segments.zh: 我也不知道，但重要的是要知道它们非常快，然后下降，然后它们上升。

segments.en: They have to take Saint Nicholas to the roof of the house, on top of the house.
segments.zh: 他们必须将圣尼古拉斯带到房子的顶部，在房子的顶部。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So now he arrives to the top of the house, line 32.
segments.zh: 所以现在他到达了房子的顶部，第 32 行。

segments.en: We see, down the chimney, Saint Nicholas came with a bound.
segments.zh: 我们看到，在烟囱下，圣尼古拉斯带着一个被束缚来了。

segments.en: He came quickly, down the chimney, boom.
segments.zh: 他很快就来了，顺着烟囱，轰隆隆。

segments.en: And at the end, he's all dressed in fur from his head to his foot.
segments.zh: 最后，他从头到脚都穿着毛皮。

segments.en: So top to bottom, he has fur on.
segments.zh: 所以从上到下，他穿着毛皮。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And I think he's got fur because he lives in the North Pole, right?
segments.zh: 而且我认为他有毛皮是因为他住在北极，对吧？

segments.en: That's right. And it's very cold where Santa Claus lives, so he has to wear these clothes that are very warm.
segments.zh: 没错。 圣诞老人住的地方很冷，所以他必须穿这些很温暖的衣服。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And obviously, since he is going up and down chimneys in line 34, we see, and his clothes were tarnished with ashes and soot.
segments.zh: 显然，由于他在 34 号线上上下下烟囱，我们看到，他的衣服被灰烬和烟尘玷污了。

segments.en: So to tarnish or tarnish means dirty.
segments.zh: 所以失去或玷污意味着肮脏。

segments.en: Something is tarnished if it's dirty.
segments.zh: 如果它脏了，东西就会被玷污。

segments.en: So his clothes, his fur clothes were dirty with ashes and soot.
segments.zh: 所以他的衣服，他的毛皮衣服上沾满了灰烬和烟灰。

segments.en: This means that, you know, in your fireplace, when the fire is gone, there's some gray and black stuff.
segments.zh: 这意味着，你知道，在你的壁炉里，当火消失时，有一些灰色和黑色的东西。

segments.en: And that's what's on Santa Claus' clothes.
segments.zh: 这就是圣诞老人衣服上的东西。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: So, and then we go on to line 35, a bundle of toys he had flung on his back.
segments.zh: 所以，然后我们继续前往第 35 行，这是一捆他背在背上的玩具。

segments.en: And he looked like a peddler just opening his pack.
segments.zh: 他看起来像个小贩，只是打开他的背包。

segments.en: All right, a peddler.
segments.zh: 好吧，一个小贩。

segments.en: Now, this is not just something we talk about on Christmas.
segments.zh: 现在，这不仅仅是我们在圣诞节谈论的事情。

segments.en: You know, we have peddlers all year round.
segments.zh: 你知道，我们一年四季都有小贩。

segments.en: What are peddlers? What do they do?
segments.zh: 什么是小贩？ 他们是做什么的？

segments.en: Basically, they go around selling things.
segments.zh: 基本上，他们到处卖东西。

segments.en: So maybe you see them in a small market or sometimes in different places and maybe, I don't know, on the streets.
segments.zh: 所以也许你在一个小市场或有时在不同的地方看到它们，也许，我不知道，在街上。

segments.en: You see them selling little things like toys or combs or books, something like that.
segments.zh: 你看到他们卖小东西，比如玩具、梳子或书籍，类似的东西。

segments.en: Oranges, you see fruit peddlers, people who sell fruit.
segments.zh: 橙子，你看到水果小贩，卖水果的人。

segments.en: Or you can see those watch peddlers.
segments.zh: 或者你可以看到那些手表小贩。

segments.en: You know, they say, would you like a Rolex watch?
segments.zh: 你知道，他们说，你想要一块劳力士手表吗？

segments.en: That's a watch peddler.
segments.zh: 那是一个手表小贩。

segments.en: So that's what they do, right?
segments.zh: 所以这就是他们所做的，对吧？

segments.en: They're informal salesmen.
segments.zh: 他们是非正式的推销员。

segments.en: They don't have a store.
segments.zh: 他们没有商店。

segments.en: They work on the street.
segments.zh: 他们在街上工作。

segments.en: So this is why Santa looks like a peddler.
segments.zh: 所以这就是为什么圣诞老人看起来像个小贩。

segments.en: He isn't in a store.
segments.zh: 他不在商店里。

segments.en: He has a bag.
segments.zh: 他有一个包。

segments.en: And he says, look in my bag.
segments.zh: 他说，看看我的包。

segments.en: Right, exactly.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: From line 37, we go on to describe the way Santa Claus looks like.
segments.zh: 从第 37 行，我们继续描述圣诞老人的样子。

segments.en: So he says, his eyes, how they twinkled.
segments.zh: 所以他说，他的眼睛，它们是如何闪烁的。

segments.en: His dimples, how merry.
segments.zh: 他的酒窝，多么快乐。

segments.en: Dimples are those small circles on your cheeks.
segments.zh: 酒窝是你脸颊上的那些小圆圈。

segments.en: So some people, when they smile, they have these small holes or circles.
segments.zh: 所以有些人，当他们微笑时，他们有这些小洞或圆圈。

segments.en: Those are dimples.
segments.zh: 那些是酒窝。

segments.en: They're very cute.
segments.zh: 他们非常可爱。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So not everyone has them, right?
segments.zh: 所以不是每个人都有，对吧？

segments.en: Some people, when they smile, you can see those dimples.
segments.zh: 有些人，当他们微笑时，你可以看到那些酒窝。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And his cheeks were like roses, his nose like a cherry.
segments.zh: 他的脸颊像玫瑰，鼻子像樱桃。

segments.en: So we're saying that they're red.
segments.zh: 所以我们说它们是红色的。

segments.en: They're red.
segments.zh: 他们是红色的。

segments.en: They're pink.
segments.zh: 他们是粉红色的。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Now in line 39, he says, his droll little mouth was drawn up like a bow.
segments.zh: 他说，现在在第 39 行，他滑稽的小嘴像弓一样拉起。

segments.en: Now, droll is a word that some people still use.
segments.zh: 现在，droll 是一些人仍然使用的一个词。

segments.en: It's pretty common in places like England.
segments.zh: 在英国这样的地方很常见。

segments.en: We don't use it as much in America.
segments.zh: 在美国，我们没有那么多地使用它。

segments.en: We say funny instead.
segments.zh: 我们说有趣。

segments.en: But something that is droll, D-R-O-L-L, droll is funny.
segments.zh: 但是一些滑稽的东西，d-r-o-l-l，droll 很有趣。

segments.en: So his mouth, his face is funny looking.
segments.zh: 所以他的嘴巴，他的脸看起来很有趣。

segments.en: Okay. His face is funny looking. All right.
segments.zh: 好的。 他的脸看起来很有趣。 好的。

segments.en: And going on to line 45, we're describing how he was chubby and plump.
segments.zh: 在第 45 行，我们正在描述他是如何胖乎乎的和丰满的。

segments.en: So we're basically saying he was a little bit fat.
segments.zh: 所以我们基本上是说他有点胖。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: A right jolly old elf.
segments.zh: 一个快乐的老精灵。

segments.en: So what is an elf?
segments.zh: 那么什么是精灵？

segments.en: An elf is actually normally we talk about elves.
segments.zh: 精灵实际上是我们谈论的精灵。

segments.en: So one elf, two elves as people, little people who help Santa.
segments.zh: 所以一个精灵，两个精灵作为人，帮助圣诞老人的小人。

segments.en: They're mythical creatures who live in the North Pole and who make presents.
segments.zh: 他们是住在北极并做礼物的神话生物。

segments.en: So an elf is a small creature who makes presents.
segments.zh: 所以精灵是一个小生物，会做礼物。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Or maybe lives in the woods.
segments.zh: 或者也许住在树林里。

segments.en: There are many different stories with elves.
segments.zh: 精灵有许多不同的故事。

segments.en: Right, right. Okay.
segments.zh: 对，对。 好的。

segments.en: And in line 46, we say, and I laughed when I saw him in spite of myself.
segments.zh: 我们说，在第 46 行，当我看到他时，我还是笑了。

segments.en: What does he mean by in spite of myself?
segments.zh: 他是什么意思？

segments.en: This is really important and this is something we say in English all the time, in spite of myself.
segments.zh: 这非常重要，这是我们一直用英语说的话，尽管我自己。

segments.en: So I laughed in spite of myself.
segments.zh: 所以我不由自主地笑了。

segments.en: So I didn't want to laugh.
segments.zh: 所以我不想笑。

segments.en: But I did.
segments.zh: 但我做到了。

segments.en: I wanted to be serious.
segments.zh: 我想认真。

segments.en: But I did laugh.
segments.zh: 但我确实笑了。

segments.en: So in spite of myself, I didn't want to laugh.
segments.zh: 所以尽管我自己，我不想笑。

segments.en: I laughed anyway.
segments.zh: 反正我笑了。

segments.en: So you say in spite of myself when you did the thing you did not want to do.
segments.zh: 所以你在做你不想做的事情时自言自语。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And finishing off, we are going towards the last three lines where we say, and away they all flew like the down of a thistle.
segments.zh: 最后，我们将走向我们所说的最后三行，然后它们都像飞蓟一样飞翔。

segments.en: What is a thistle?
segments.zh: 什么是蓟？

segments.en: They're talking about the part of a flower that's a thistle.
segments.zh: 他们在谈论一朵花的部分是蓟。

segments.en: Oh, okay.
segments.zh: 哦，好吧。

segments.en: So they just, they all flew away like quickly, rapidly like the little flower.
segments.zh: 所以他们只是，他们都像小花一样迅速飞走。

segments.en: Well, you know when a flower is sending its seeds out, it's down, it's white.
segments.zh: 好吧，你知道什么时候一朵花把它的种子送出去，它倒下了，它是白色的。

segments.en: So maybe if you blow on a flower with the white seeds, they blow away.
segments.zh: 所以也许如果你用白色的种子吹一朵花，它们就会被吹走。

segments.en: That's what it looks like.
segments.zh: 这就是它的样子。

segments.en: It looks like the seeds of a flower being blown away.
segments.zh: 它看起来像一朵花的种子被吹走了。

segments.en: Very easy.
segments.zh: 很容易。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Line 55 says, but I heard him exclaim, ere he drove out of sight.
segments.zh: 第 55 行说，但我听到他惊呼，在他开车看不见的地方。

segments.en: So this is an older way of saying, as he drove out of sight.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种古老的说法，因为他开车离开了视线。

segments.en: So as he's flying away, I can't see him anymore.
segments.zh: 所以当他飞走时，我再也看不到他了。

segments.en: Almost I can't see him anymore.
segments.zh: 几乎我再也见不到他了。

segments.en: He exclaimed something.
segments.zh: 他惊呼什么。

segments.en: So ere means while this is happening.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着在这发生的时候。

segments.en: Now this is another one of those maybe old English words that we don't use anymore, right?
segments.zh: 现在这是另一个我们不再使用的可能古英语单词，对吧？

segments.en: You wouldn't really use ere.
segments.zh: 你不会真正使用 ere。

segments.en: Ere I was walking to school, I saw the milkman.
segments.zh: 在我走路去学校之前，我看到了送奶工。

segments.en: No, we don't say this anymore.
segments.zh: 不，我们不再说这个了。

segments.en: But you will find it in poetry and you might also find it in stories.
segments.zh: 但你会在诗歌中找到它，你也可能在故事中找到它。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And line 56, he ends and this is very the famous way that this poem ends by saying, Happy Christmas to all and to all a good night.
segments.zh: 第 56 行，他结束了，这就是这首诗的著名方式，祝大家圣诞快乐，祝大家晚安。

segments.en: Happy Christmas to all and to all a good night.
segments.zh: 祝大家圣诞快乐，祝大家晚安。

segments.en: Yeah, this is the, and the first line of the poem are the most famous.
segments.zh: 是的，这就是这首诗的第一行，也是最著名的。

segments.en: Everyone knows these.
segments.zh: 大家都知道这些。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So a beautiful poem.
segments.zh: 所以一首美丽的诗。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to it one more time?
segments.zh: 我们为什么不再听一遍？

segments.en: 'Twas the night before Christmas, when all through the house, not a creature was stirring, not even a mouse.
segments.zh: 圣诞前夜，整座屋子静悄悄，连一只老鼠都没有动静。

segments.en: The stockings were hung by the chimney with care, in hopes that St. Nicholas soon would be there.
segments.zh: 长袜被仔细挂在烟囱旁，盼着圣尼古拉斯快快到来。

segments.en: The children were nestled all snug in their beds, while visions of sugarplums danced in their heads.
segments.zh: 孩子们舒舒服服地睡在床上，梦里的糖李子翩翩起舞。

segments.en: And Mama in her kerchief and I in my cap had just settled down for a long winter's nap.
segments.zh: 妈妈裹着头巾，我戴着睡帽，刚躺下准备睡个漫长的冬夜觉。

segments.en: When out on the lawn there arose such a clatter, I sprang from the bed to see what was the matter.
segments.zh: 草坪上突然传来一阵喧闹，我从床上一跃而起，想看个究竟。

segments.en: Away to the window I flew like a flash, tore open the shutters and threw open the sash.
segments.zh: 我闪电般冲到窗边，猛地推开百叶窗，拉起窗框。

segments.en: The moon on the breast of the new fallen snow gave the luster of midday to objects below.
segments.zh: 新下雪的乳房上的月亮给下面的物体带来了中午的光泽。

segments.en: When what to my wondering eyes should appear but a miniature sleigh, and eight tiny reindeer, with a little old driver, so lively and quick, I knew in a moment it must be St. Nick.
segments.zh: 当我想知道的眼睛只出现一辆微型雪橇和八只小驯鹿时，有一个小老司机，如此活泼和快速，我知道它一定是圣尼克。

segments.en: More rapid than eagles his coursers they came, and he whistled and shouted and called them by name.
segments.zh: 驯鹿快过雄鹰奔来，他吹着口哨，高声喊出它们的名字。

segments.en: Now Dasher, now Dancer, now Prancer and Vixen, on Comet, on Cupid, on Donder and Blitzen.
segments.zh: 现在达舍，现在是舞者，现在是普兰克和狐狸精，在彗星上，在丘比特上，在唐德和布尔泽恩。

segments.en: To the top of the porch, to the top of the wall, now dash away, dash away, dash away all.
segments.zh: 到门廊的顶部，到墙的顶部，现在冲走，冲走，冲破一切。

segments.en: As dry leaves that before the wild hurricanes fly, when they meet with an obstacle, mount to the sky.
segments.zh: 它们像狂风中翻飞的枯叶，遇到障碍便腾上天空。

segments.en: So up to the housetop the coursers they flew with the sleighs full of toys, and St. Nicholas too.
segments.zh: 所以到房子顶部的课程，他们带着装满玩具的雪橇和圣尼古拉斯飞了起来。

segments.en: And then, in a twinkling, I heard on the roof, the prancing and pawing of each little hoof.
segments.zh: 然后，在闪烁中，我在屋顶上听到了每个小蹄子的腾跃和爪子。

segments.en: As I drew in my head and was turning around, down the chimney St. Nicholas came with a bound.
segments.zh: 我刚把头缩回来、转过身，圣尼古拉斯就一跃而下，从烟囱里钻了出来。

segments.en: He was dressed all in fur from his head to his toe, and his clothes were all tarnished with ashes and soot.
segments.zh: 他从头到脚裹着毛皮，衣服沾满了灰烬和煤烟。

segments.en: A bundle of toys he had flung on his back, and he looked like a peddler just opening his pack.
segments.zh: 他背着一大袋玩具，像个刚打开货包的小贩。

segments.en: His eyes, how they twinkled! His dimples, how merry!
segments.zh: 他的眼睛闪闪发亮，酒窝里满是笑意。

segments.en: His cheeks were like roses, his nose like a cherry.
segments.zh: 他的双颊红如玫瑰，鼻子红如樱桃。

segments.en: His droll little mouth was drawn up in a bow, and the beard of his chin was as white as the snow.
segments.zh: 他俏皮的小嘴弯成弓形，下巴上的胡子白得像雪。

segments.en: The stump of a pipe he held tight in his teeth, and the smoke had encircled his head like a wreath.
segments.zh: 他紧紧地咬在牙齿上的烟斗的残端，烟雾像花环一样环绕着他的头。

segments.en: He had a broad face and a little round belly that shook when he laughed like a bowl full of jelly.
segments.zh: 他有张宽脸和圆鼓鼓的小肚子，一笑起来就像一碗果冻般颤动。

segments.en: He was chubby and plump, a right old jolly elf, and I laughed when I saw him, in spite of myself.
segments.zh: 他又胖又胖，是个快乐的老小精灵，我看到他时还是笑了，尽管我自己。

segments.en: A wink of his eye and a twist of his head soon gave me to know I had nothing to dread.
segments.zh: 他眨眨眼、歪歪头，立刻让我知道无需害怕。

segments.en: He spoke not a word, but went straight to work and filled all the stockings, then turned with a jerk, and laying his finger aside of his nose and giving a nod, up the chimney he rose.
segments.zh: 他一句话也没说，而是直接上班，把所有的长袜都装满了，然后猛地转过身来，把手指放在鼻子旁边，点了点头，抬起了他升起的烟囱。

segments.en: He sprang to his sleigh, to his team gave a whistle, and away they all flew like the down of a thistle.
segments.zh: 他跃上雪橇，向驯鹿吹声口哨，大家像蓟花绒毛一样飘飞远去。

segments.en: But I heard him exclaim, ere as he drove out of sight, Happy Christmas to all, and to all a good night!
segments.zh: 但我听到他惊呼，当他开车离开视线时，祝大家圣诞快乐，祝大家晚安！

segments.en: It's very interesting because it's part of the American tradition of Christmas.
segments.zh: 这很有趣，因为它是美国圣诞节传统的一部分。

segments.en: I think maybe also in other parts of the world the poem might be translated or also might be popular.
segments.zh: 我想也许在世界其他地方，这首诗可能会被翻译或也可能很受欢迎。

segments.en: But you know, Santa Claus and all these things are traditions that are observed in some countries and it's very interesting to understand them.
segments.zh: 但你知道，圣诞老人和所有这些都是在一些国家观察到的传统，理解它们是非常有趣的。

segments.en: Absolutely, and I'm very curious to know about your Christmas traditions.
segments.zh: 当然，我很想知道你的圣诞节传统。

segments.en: What do you do in your home country on Christmas Eve or on Christmas Day?
segments.zh: 圣诞节前夕或圣诞节，你在你的祖国做什么？

segments.en: Do you know any poems like this or do you listen to this poem in translation?
segments.zh: 你知道这样的诗还是你在翻译中听这首诗？

segments.en: Let us know.
segments.zh: 告诉我们吧。

segments.en: Our website is EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 我们的网站是 EnglishPod.com。

segments.en: Alright guys, we'll see you there and have a Merry Christmas.
segments.zh: 好吧，伙计们，我们会在那里见到你们，圣诞快乐。

segments.en: Merry Christmas.
segments.zh: 圣诞快乐。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
